page.layout: One printed page. Running head "ITALIA." at top with page number 55 at top right. Main text in one column of verse and prose, with a heading "Montes Italiae praeter Apenninum." and subheadings in the middle and lower part. Marginal notes in the right margin, beside the verse lines. Signature "D 4" at the foot.

p.i: Æstuat, & stygios exalat in aëra flatus.
Spelunca alta fuit, vastoque immanis hiatu,
Scrupea, tuta lacu nigro, nemorumque tenebris,
Quam super haud ulla poterant impune volantes
Tendere iter pennis: talis sese halitus atris
Faucibus effundens supera ad connexa ferebat:
Unde locum Graij dixerunt nomine Avernum.
Marisque Baijs obstrepentis vrges summouere littora,
Quid referam Baias, praeextaque littora velis.
Et qua de calido sulfure fumat, aquam?
Enthea fatidicae seu visere tecta Sibyllae
Dulce sit, iliacoque iugum memorabile remo.

main_text.head: Montes Italiae praeter Apenninum.
Garganus mons seu promontorium Apuliae.
main_text.p: Claudian. de 4. Honorij consulatu. Horat. carm. lib. 2.

page.notes: Marginal notes at right are partly faint and the placement of the note letters is approximate. Some words in the verse are doubtful due to the scan (e.g. "vsti[?]sque", "Querceta"). Greek word "Æstuat" and the Greek-letter mark "Rumpere" line are approximate.
